drug_class: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor (SSRI) — a type of antidepressant
purpose: Escitalopram is used to treat depression and generalized anxiety disorder. It can help improve your mood, energy levels, sleep, and overall sense of well-being. It is also sometimes used for other anxiety-related conditions.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called serotonin to help regulate mood and emotions. Escitalopram works by keeping more serotonin available in your brain by blocking it from being reabsorbed too quickly. Think of it like keeping the happy-chemical signal going stronger and longer so your brain can work more balanced.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headache, dry mouth, sweating, trouble sleeping or feeling sleepy, and sexual side effects such as decreased sex drive. Most of these tend to improve after the first few weeks as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as it can cause withdrawal-like symptoms such as dizziness or irritability. In the first few weeks, especially in younger people under 25, watch for any increase in sad or suicidal thoughts and contact your doctor right away if this happens. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some combinations can be dangerous.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg taken once a day, either in the morning or evening, with or without food. Your doctor may increase the dose to 20 mg per day after at least one week if needed. It can take 2 to 4 weeks before you start feeling the full benefit, so be patient and keep taking it as directed.
